title: Weekend batch June 7-8 posted duplicate legs: replay and Monday catch-up both ran
subtitle: 62,104 duplicate postings, caught Monday June 9 06:19 ET. Exception queue noise. No customer cash movement (held). Blameless. Lock on batch_id. Page Saturday if anyone replays.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Priya Nair (EM), Helen Cho (ops), Diego Alvarez (SRE), weekend on-call rotation. Copy Rahul Deshmukh and Marcus Bell.
owners: Aman Kumar (postmortem, batch_id lock), Priya Nair (action tracking), Helen Cho (replay UI acceptance)
summary: On Saturday June 7, 2025 Helen Cho's ops team ran a manual replay of weekend batch BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND because the replay UI did not show that the batch had already landed. The Monday June 9 05:30 ET catch-up job, which treats Saturday and Sunday as dark unless a catch-up flag is set, posted the same legs again. 62,104 duplicate postings hit break.exception_queue. Caught 06:19 ET Monday when depth jumped from 388 to 41,206. All duplicates were held (status EXC-DUP); no customer cash movement. Blameless: the on-call (Lena Ortiz) reasonably treated weekends as dark per CLH-SOP-2023-028; the UI never said already landed; catch-up and replay did not share a lock on batch_id. Actions: unique lock on batch_id in the poster, Saturday pager when a replay starts, UI badge. This write-up is the record, not a hunt for who clicked.
form_description: Blameless incident postmortem for the June 7-8 2025 Clearhaven weekend batch that double-posted 62,104 legs after a manual replay and the Monday catch-up both ran. Impact was exception-queue noise; cash was held.
revision_history: Same-day timeline from Slack, PagerDuty, and Postgres. Not yet reviewed.
Helen and Lena reviewed. Removed a sentence that read like blame for the Saturday click. Added UI screenshots notes (no screenshots in this JSON).
Priya accepted actions and dates. Marcus confirmed no counterparty cash file went out.
Approved for the Monday incident review. Action tickets CH-BAT-3310, CH-BAT-3314, CH-OPS-4419.

blocks.text: Summary for people who will not read the timeline

blocks.label: What we are changing
blocks.text: 1) Poster takes an advisory lock and a unique write on batch_id before inserting legs; a second poster for the same batch_id exits 0 with a log line already_landed, it does not insert. 2) Starting a replay on Saturday or Sunday pages match-engine-prod, even if the on-call runbook still says weekends are dark. 3) Replay UI shows already landed / in flight / not found, from recon.batch_landing, not from the operator's memory. We are not punishing the Saturday replay. We are not turning off Monday catch-up. We are not calling this a cash incident.

Sev-2, not Sev-1. Customer cash did not move. The posting path writes to break.leg_status and, on success, to post.outbound_queue. Duplicates hit a check we added in 2024 after a smaller weekday double-click (CH-BAT-1188, 2,041 rows, April 2024). That check named them EXC-DUP and skipped outbound_queue. It worked. Helen's queue was unusable until 11:40 ET Monday while we bulk-closed EXC-DUP. Ops pain is real. Counterparties did not see a second settlement file. Marcus checked RailClear and two other TAMs. File counts for Monday morning matched T-1 within 0.3%.
Impact

rows: COUNT(*) FROM break.exception_queue WHERE status='EXC-DUP' AND opened_at >= '2025-06-09 05:30' AND opened_at < '2025-06-09 06:25'

blocks.text: What customers and counterparties saw: a slower ops response on unrelated OPEN breaks until 11:40, because the queue UI paginates 50 rows and EXC-DUP drowned everything. Helen's team worked the real OPEN set from a SQL filter she already had (status IN ('OPEN','EXC-HOLD')). We will give that filter a button. That is an action, not a hero story. RailClear's 16:00 file Monday was on time. No TAM email went out. Marcus drafted one and Priya killed it: we do not announce a non-event to counterparties.
Timeline

All times Eastern. Saturday June 7, Sunday June 8, Monday June 9, 2025. Weekend on-call was Lena Ortiz (SE II, rotation per CLH-SOP-2023-028). I was backup. Helen's Saturday coverage was herself plus two ops analysts (Priya G. and Dan Holt, Clearhaven ops; not Northstar). I was not in Slack Saturday. That is a fact, not an excuse; the pager did not fire Saturday because nothing we watch fired.

blocks.caption: Timeline. Slack quotes paraphrased. PagerDuty and Postgres timestamps are exact.
rows: Friday close file sent. Helen notes 2,412 EXC-HOLD on a late RailClear restatement, unrelated to weekend batch, ticket CH-OPS-4412. They plan to replay that RailClear slice Monday if still open. This is background, not the incident.

Weekend inbound BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND lands from the Saturday counterparties (four firms that trade late Friday). land-api produces 62,104 legs onto clh.settlement.inbound. recon.batch_landing row created: status=landed, landed_at=09:14:22.

match-engine consumes, posts, ack. batch_landing.status=posted, posted_at=10:02:18, posted_by=job:match-engine. This is a successful first post. No page. Weekend dashboards are thin; ingest-kafka-lag never crossed 50k.

Helen opens replay UI (https://replay.prod.clearhaven.internal, CLH-PRD-2024-002). She is looking for the Friday RailClear slice. Search by date 2025-06-07 (she wanted Friday's late file; the date picker defaults to 'today'). UI lists BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND with columns batch_id, leg_count, landed_at. Column posted_at exists in the API and is not rendered. Status column shows landed, which in this UI means 'we have a landing row,' not 'not yet posted.' Helen reads it as not posted.

Helen confirms with Priya G. The Saturday file 'looks stuck at landed.' Dan Holt says the old SFTP drop is empty, which is true because Kafka is the default path. Empty SFTP is not evidence the batch failed.

Helen clicks Replay on BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND, ticket CH-OPS-4419 (created at 11:38, comment 'weekend batch not posted, replay'). Replay job job:batch-replay starts, actor Helen, no pager. CLH-SOP-2023-028 still says page on replay during 07:00-19:00 weekdays only. Saturday is outside that.

Replay re-produces 62,104 messages with the same leg_id and the same batch_id. ingest-api idempotency on (leg_id, batch_id) drops 61,891 as duplicates at ingest (good). 213 legs had a batch_id suffix the replay job added historically for 'replay attempts' (_r1). Those 213 ingest as new. Small, we will come back to them. The other 61,891 never reach match-engine again. Replay job logs 'produced 62104, ingest ack 213 new, 61891 dup.' Nobody reads the log on Saturday. The UI shows replay status=success because the job exited 0.

Helen sees success, closes CH-OPS-4419 as done. Queue depth Saturday 12:15 is 401, not exciting. The 213 _r1 legs post as new and are real extras, not the 62,104. They sit as OPEN, mixed with Friday's EXC-HOLD.
Dark. No catch-up. No replay. Lena's pager quiet. batch_landing still status=posted from 10:02 Saturday.

CronJob weekend-catchup (helm release ingest-api, schedule 30 9 * * 1 UTC = 05:30 ET in June) starts. Purpose: post Saturday/Sunday batches that are landed but not posted, because historically weekend match-engine was down (2019-2023). Match-engine has been up on weekends since the EKS move (2024). The catch-up job was never killed. Its query is: SELECT batch_id FROM recon.batch_landing WHERE batch_date IN (last Saturday, last Sunday) AND status <> 'catchup_done'. It does not look at status=posted. posted and catchup_done are different values. BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND is posted, so it matches <> catchup_done. The job treats it as needs posting.
Catch-up calls the same poster path as replay, with a different producer id job:weekend-catchup. It does not add _r1. It re-produces 62,104 messages with original leg_id + original batch_id.

ingest-api idempotency on (leg_id, batch_id) should drop these. It does not, because the poster path catch-up uses is post.force_reissue=true, a flag meant for Helen's 'replay this, I know it is a duplicate, I need a new outbound' which we never documented as catch-up's flag. Catch-up inherited it from a 2024 copy-paste in the CronJob args (values-prod.yaml, line comment 'same as replay'). Replay on Saturday did not set force_reissue (UI default false). Catch-up set it true. ingest writes a second raw_leg with a new ingest_id, same leg_id, same batch_id.

match-engine posts the second copy. Unique check on (leg_id, batch_id) for outbound_queue fires. Insert skipped. Row written to exception_queue status=EXC-DUP. 62,104 times. Each insert is fast. Queue depth climbs ~1,100 rows/minute.

Alert ExceptionQueueDepthHigh, threshold 5,000. PagerDuty match-engine-prod. Lena acks 06:20:14. Helen is already in #clh-ops at 06:18 because her hourly mail at 06:15 said depth 28,440 and she thought the mail was wrong.

Aman joins (backup). Depth 62,492. Kavya joins 06:27. We pause the CronJob: kubectl -n clh-ingest scale cronjob/weekend-catchup --replicas=0 is wrong (CronJobs do not scale that way); kubectl -n clh-ingest patch cronjob weekend-catchup -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'. Job pod already completed. Pause is for next Monday.

Kavya's query shows all new rows EXC-DUP, same batch_id, opened_at in 05:31-06:18. outbound_queue inserts for that batch_id Monday = 0. I say held. Helen wants that in writing before she tells her head of ops. I write it in the channel 06:44.
Marcus confirms no extra files at RailClear. Priya opens Sev-2 retroactively to 06:19.

Bulk close EXC-DUP for that batch_id after Sneha samples 200 rows. Queue depth 612 at 11:40. Sev-2 closed 11:42. Remaining OPEN includes Friday's 2,412 EXC-HOLD and the 213 _r1 extras, which we then suppress under CH-OPS-4419 (reopened) after Helen confirms they are replay artifacts.
We leave weekend-catchup suspended. This postmortem. Staging repro of force_reissue + posted-but-not-catchup_done.

blocks.text: What actually failed (systems, not people)
1. Replay UI did not show already landed / already posted

recon.batch_landing had posted_at=10:02:18 Saturday. The UI list view (ReplaySearch.tsx, last touched March 2025 for the date picker) renders batch_id, leg_count, landed_at, and a status badge that maps any row existence to the word landed. posted_at is in the JSON and ignored. There is no badge for posted, no badge for catchup_done, no warning on the Replay button. Helen used the product we shipped. The Friday RailClear slice she meant to find is BATCH-2025-06-06-RC-LATE, which was on the previous calendar date; the default date picker hid it. That is two UI bugs stacked: wrong default date for 'what I am likely replaying on a Saturday morning' and a status word that lies.
2. Weekend catch-up still assumes dark weekends

CLH-SOP-2023-028, written when match-engine was 18 EC2 pets and we often left it scaled down Saturday, says on-call may treat weekends as dark unless paged. The CronJob weekend-catchup was the compensating control: Monday morning, post whatever landed over the weekend. After EKS, match-engine runs 12 replicas all weekend. Saturday 09:14-10:02 posted the batch for real. Catch-up still ran. Its WHERE clause never got a 'already posted' predicate. The comment in values-prod.yaml even says 'same as replay' and sets force_reissue=true, which is the opposite of a cautious catch-up. Nobody owns a yearly review of compensating CronJobs after the thing they compensate for goes away. That is on the platform, which is me and Diego and Priya, not Lena.
3. No lock on batch_id

Two posters can run for one batch_id. Replay and catch-up are different binaries with the same Kafka produce path. ingest idempotency works when force_reissue is false. Catch-up turns it off. There is no Postgres advisory lock, no INSERT INTO recon.batch_post_lock (batch_id) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, no 'if posted_at is not null then exit.' The 2024 EXC-DUP check is a seatbelt after the insert into exception_queue. Seatbelts are good. They are not locks. 62,104 seatbelt events is how you notice you needed a lock.
4. Saturday replay did not page

Lena did not know a replay ran. SOP said not to expect weekend replay. The replay job has a Slack mention to #clh-ingest, which fired Saturday 11:41. #clh-ingest is not a pager. Lena is in #clh-oncall and PagerDuty. Helen is in #clh-ops. Three channels, none of them required a human on the engineering side to look at a Saturday replay. If we had been looking, we might have seen the 213 _r1 extras and asked questions. We would not have stopped Monday catch-up, because we would have had to know the WHERE clause was wrong. Pager on replay is still the right change: it puts a person in the loop before Monday.
5. The 213 _r1 extras (small, same family)

Replay job still suffixes _r1 on a code path we thought we deleted in January 2025 (CH-BAT-2801). 213 legs had a producer-side mutation of batch_id when a metric label overflowed and a fallback formatter ran. They ingested as new, posted as new, cash still held because they did not match street-side. They added noise. Fix the formatter. Do not let a metric label change a business key. That sentence is going on a lint rule if I can find one that works.
Contributing factors

items: SOP CLH-SOP-2023-028 weekend=dark, never revised after EKS always-on (CLH-MEM-2023-027, 2023, soak into 2024). Stale SOP plus a leftover CronJob is a pattern. We should grep for other leftover catch-ups (Diego took that, see actions).

Replay UI built from CLH-PRD-2024-002 happy path (weekday, batch not yet posted). posted_at was in the API for the audit trail work (CLH-REQ-2022-033 era fields on landing, later). UI never consumed it.
force_reissue=true on catch-up from a values-prod.yaml copy-paste, no review in 2025 helm diffs because the line did not change. Unchanged bad config is invisible in review.
Date picker default 'today' on a Saturday morning when ops is usually thinking about Friday. Helen's intent was Friday RailClear. The product did not help her get there.

ExceptionQueueDepthHigh threshold 5,000. Fine for weekday. We did not have a weekend-specific threshold. Not a cause of the duplicates. It is why we caught at 06:19 instead of 06:15 (Helen's mail) or 05:45 (if we had watched catch-up logs). Detection was acceptable. Prevention was not.

blocks.text: What we considered and rejected

blocks.caption: So the retro does not reopen these as if they were new ideas.
rows: Delete Monday catch-up CronJob and rely on always-on match-engine
Catch-up is still the right safety if we ever scale match-engine to 0 on a holiday. Keep the job, fix the WHERE clause and the lock. Do not delete the spare tire; stop it from inflating twice.
Helen will replay on weekends when a file is actually stuck. Ban pushes it to SSH and SQL. We page instead, we do not ban.
Treat this as a cash incident and notify counterparties
Zero outbound duplicates. Priya: no email. Marcus agreed after the query.
Have on-call sit the replay UI every Saturday 09:00-13:00
That is a staffing tax for a badge and a pager we can ship in a week. No.
Make EXC-DUP auto-close so the queue never shows them
Then we would not have seen 62,104. The seatbelt would be silent. Keep EXC-DUP visible, add a filter button, bulk-close remains a deliberate step.

blocks.text: Corrective actions

blocks.caption: Dated. Priya tracks. If a date moves, the ticket moves, not this paragraph in Slack.
rows: Lock on batch_id: INSERT recon.batch_post_lock (batch_id, locked_by, locked_at) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING; poster exits if no row. Unique on batch_id. Catch-up and replay both use it. force_reissue cannot skip the lock; it can only skip ingest idempotency after a lock is held by the same actor with an explicit ticket.
Staging: two posters, one inserts, one exits already_landed. Sneha AT. Prod helm upgrade not on a Friday.
Catch-up WHERE status = 'landed' AND posted_at IS NULL. Remove force_reissue from CronJob args. Comment in values-prod.yaml that says 'same as replay' deleted.
Staging catch-up on a posted batch is a no-op. CronJob unsuspended after that, not before.

Replay list: columns posted_at, posted_by, badges posted / in flight / landed-not-posted. Replay button disabled when posted unless the operator types the batch_id a second time (Helen asked for a typed confirm, not a hidden click).
Helen clicks through a staging posted batch and cannot one-click replay it.
Date picker: Saturday/Sunday default to previous Friday plus a 'weekend batches' chip. Do not default to today on weekend.
Same accept session as the badge.
Replay start pages match-engine-prod on Saturday and Sunday (and weekday 19:00-07:00). Slack #clh-oncall plus PagerDuty. Dedup 30 min so retries do not page-storm.
Staging page to the empty rotation, then prod. Lena verifies from the next weekend rotation.
Grep leftover catch-up / compensating CronJobs that mention dark, weekend, or scale-to-0. List in CH-BAT-3321, kill or fix each.
List reviewed with Priya. No silent jobs.
Weekends are not dark. Replay pages. Catch-up is last-resort for landed-not-posted only.
SOP diff linked from this incident.
Stop _r1 suffix on replay. Business keys are not metric labels.
Unit test: formatter cannot mutate batch_id.
Queue UI: saved filter Hide EXC-DUP. Bulk close remains a separate, ticketed action.
Helen uses it on a noisy day without SQL.

blocks.text: Detection and response: what went well

EXC-DUP held cash. That check is the reason this is a queue incident and not a street incident. Credit the 2024 work (CH-BAT-1188) and Sneha's tests that we did not skip when it felt like a small weekday bug.
Helen's 06:15 hourly mail beat the pager by four minutes. Keep the mail. Threshold 5,000 on the pager is still fine; do not lower it to 400 or we page every month-end.
Lena acked in 67 seconds and did not helm rollback. Rollback was the wrong tool (see CLH-RB-2024-011). She patched the CronJob suspend with Diego on the call. That was the right containment.
Marcus checked outbound before anyone drafted a customer sentence. Order of operations was impact, then words.
Engineer appendix: queries and containment commands
For the next person. Postgres clh-recon-prod, role oncall_ro for SELECT, break_app is not to be used from a laptop. Containment commands are cluster clh-prod-eks-01.

blocks.caption: Queries we ran Monday morning, plus the CronJob suspend. Do not bulk-close EXC-DUP without Helen.

-- depth and status mix
SELECT status, COUNT(*) 
FROM break.exception_queue
WHERE opened_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-09 05:00:00-04'
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY 2 DESC;

-- is this one batch?
SELECT batch_id, COUNT(*) 
FROM break.exception_queue
WHERE status = 'EXC-DUP'
  AND opened_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-09 05:00:00-04'
GROUP BY batch_id;

-- landing vs posted
SELECT batch_id, status, landed_at, posted_at, posted_by, leg_count
FROM recon.batch_landing
WHERE batch_id = 'BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND';

-- outbound: must be zero extras
SELECT COUNT(*) 
FROM post.outbound_queue
WHERE batch_id = 'BATCH-2025-06-07-WKND'
  AND created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-09 05:00:00-04';

-- containment (once, then stop)
# kubectl config use-context arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:184920337661:cluster/clh-prod-eks-01
# kubectl -n clh-ingest patch cronjob weekend-catchup --type merge -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
# kubectl -n clh-ingest get cronjob weekend-catchup -o yaml | grep -A2 spec:

-- lock table we will add (do not create by hand in prod; migrate Vxx)
-- CREATE TABLE recon.batch_post_lock (
--   batch_id text PRIMARY KEY,
--   locked_by text NOT NULL,
--   locked_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
--   ticket_id text NOT NULL
-- );
How we will know this is actually fixed

Not by the absence of a matching Sev-2. By three drills. 1) Staging: land a weekend-shaped batch, let it post, run catch-up, expect 0 new exception rows and a log already_landed. 2) Staging: land, do not post, run catch-up, expect a post and posted_at set. 3) Staging: posted batch, open replay UI, button disabled until typed confirm; if someone confirms with a ticket, lock holder is replay, catch-up then no-ops. Sneha owns the drill writeup. First pass due with CH-BAT-3310. We will not unsuspend prod catch-up until drill 1 and 2 pass. Drill 3 can trail with the UI date.
Open questions

blocks.caption: Not blocking CH-BAT-3310.
rows: Are there holiday catch-ups besides weekend-catchup?
Should typed confirm on a posted replay even exist, or is that a Priya exception each time?
Helen wants the escape hatch. Priya wants a ticket id required (we already have that from CLH-REQ-2022-033). Keep hatch + ticket + lock.
Do we backfill catchup_done on historical posted weekend batches so a rogue job cannot reissue if someone reverts the WHERE clause?
I think yes, one UPDATE with Helen's OK. Count first, show her the number.
RailClear TAM curiosity: Marcus mentioned they asked why ops Slack was busy Monday. Reply?
Priya: 'internal queue, files on time' if anything. No postmortem attached.

blocks.text: Blameless close

Helen replayed a batch the UI presented as landed on a Saturday, following the play we taught ops for stuck files. Lena did not watch a weekend we told her was dark. Catch-up did the job we left in helm after the reason for the job moved out. I wrote the 2023 SOP sentence about dark weekends. I also shipped replay without posted_at on the row. That is enough ownership to go around. The useful part is the lock, the pager, the badge, and killing force_reissue on catch-up. We will review actions on July 21 in Priya's incident slot. If CH-BAT-3310 has slipped, we do not unsuspend catch-up to 'get back to normal.' Normal is what produced 62,104 EXC-DUP.
